name: Ms. Moverelli
role: Removals lady — moves what has sat on the pool long enough to the array, and leaves alone what should stay
training: Still learning: she knows the Smart Mover by heart, but hasn't moved anything on a real server yet. As soon as she has passed her test run, you can hire her.
fire_note: Letting me go stops my runs: a schedule of mine left in the office's cron file does nothing while I'm not hired (switch it off first under «Schedule» if you want it gone). A run that is going finishes its share first — I never stop a move halfway. Unraid's own mover schedule stays as it is: switch it on again under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ if you want it back.
greet.2: Old things to the array, new things stay close.
greet.3: Careful with that one, it's still in use!
greet.4: Grazie to helmi1987 — the Smart Mover is his work!
bubble.hello_short: Hello, I'm Ms. Moverelli. I move what has had its time on the pool to the array — and nothing that should stay.
bubble.loading: One moment, I'm looking at the shares…
bubble.intro: I'm Ms. Moverelli. Unraid's mover takes everything a share allows; my Smart Mover first sorts out by age, by lists of what stays and by how full the pool is — and then hands the rest to Unraid's very own move program.
bubble.unraid_old: Only: I work on Unraid {needed} and newer — this server runs {version}.
bubble.setup: Let's set it up: how old a file must be before it moves, and what always stays.
bubble.running: The Smart Mover is at work right now — I'm watching.
bubble.dry: Another mover still runs on a schedule of its own (Unraid's or Mover Tuning's) — as long as it does, I only make lists and dry runs, or we'd both move the same shares.
bubble.no_schedule: I don't run on my own yet — give me a schedule and I'll take care of it every night.
bubble.ready: All in order — I move on my schedule.
mode_hint.dry: Shows per share what would move — changes nothing.
mode_hint.run: Moves what the rules allow with Unraid's move program. Wakes the disks it moves to.
mode_hint.run_mover: Only once Unraid's own mover schedule is off (see above).
mode_hint.run_emby: Only once Jack Emby's list is among the files I leave alone (Set up…).
state_tip.moves: The Smart Mover looks at this share on every run.
state_tip.skip: Left out in my settings: the Smart Mover never touches it.
state_tip.prefer_off: This share is moved back onto its pool (prefer) — switched off in my settings.
state_tip.none: With this share's ⟦Primary storage⟧ and ⟦Secondary storage⟧ there is nothing to move: Unraid's mover leaves it alone too.
overview_sub: Unraid's mover schedule, mine, the rules for all shares and the last run.
unraid_off_sub: as it should be with me
skipped_mover: Skipped: Unraid's mover was at work for {min} min.
shares_sub: Every share as the Smart Mover sees it: where its files go (⟦Primary storage⟧ → ⟦Secondary storage⟧, or back for prefer) and which rules hold for it.
history_sub: Lists, dry runs and real runs — and the ones that didn't start, with why.
tools_sub: The Smart Mover ships with the office; it needs nothing else.
tool_sub: by helmi1987, with the office's hooks (status, stop)
credit: The Smart Mover is his work — I just carry the boxes. Under GPL-3.0.

notice.setup: Not set up yet: the rules and what always stays.
notice.running: The Smart Mover is at work ({mode}).
notice.jack_busy: One of Jack Emby's runs is going — mine wait until it is done; we never move at the same time.
notice.emby_list: Jack Emby keeps films on the pool with EmbyCache: a real run would move them back for {shares}. Add his list ({file}) to the files I leave alone.
mover.on: Unraid's own mover schedule is on ({schedule}). As long as it is, I only make lists and dry runs — otherwise both of us would move the same shares.
mover.ok: Unraid's mover schedule is off — real runs go. ⟦Move now⟧ by hand (⟦Mover Settings⟧, the ⟦Main⟧ page) still starts Unraid's mover; if it starts during my run, I stop before the next share.
mover.running: Unraid's mover is at work right now — a real run of mine waits for it.
mover.off_text: I set Unraid's own setting ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Mover schedule⟧ to ⟦Disabled⟧ and press ⟦Apply⟧ — exactly as the page does. Then my schedule moves your shares instead.
mover.off_move_now: ⟦Move now⟧ by hand stays possible; a run of mine stops before its next share then.
mover.off_back: To have it back, choose a schedule there again.
schedule.intro: When the Smart Mover runs for real on its own — once a night is right for most servers.
schedule.unraid_on: Another mover still has a schedule of its own (Unraid's or Mover Tuning's): until it is off, a scheduled run of mine is refused (and said so here).
schedule.custom_hint: A cron expression (minute hour day month weekday).
schedule.off_hint: Only when you start it here.
schedule.need_setup: Set me up first — then I can run on my own.
schedule.not_live: Saved, but Unraid hasn't taken the schedule up yet.
setup.bubble: Here are my rules: first for all shares, then whatever a share wants of its own. Nothing moves before you start it.
setup.global_sub: What holds unless a share has a rule of its own.
setup.min_age_hint: Only files that have been on the pool longer than this move. 0 = everything.
setup.min_age_prefer: Prefer shares: empty means 0 (everything comes back to the pool).
setup.age_stat_hint: ctime: since the file landed on the pool (also reset by a change of owner or rights). mtime: since it was last changed.
setup.threshold: Only when the pool is fuller than (%)
setup.threshold_hint: 0 = whatever the fill. On a ZFS pool the whole pool counts.
setup.debug: Detail of the move program's log
setup.max_list: Lines in a dry run's output
setup.max_list_hint: Per share; the log always has the full list.
setup.prefer: Bring prefer shares back to their pool
setup.prefer_hint: Like Unraid's mover: shares set to move from the array to the pool. Reads the array disks.
setup.files_hint: Files with a list each, one path per line (e.g. EmbyCache's list).
setup.patterns_hint: One per line: a folder or file (/mnt/user/…), a pattern (*.nfo) or a word in the path. # for a comment.
setup.shares_sub: Only what a share wants differently — empty means: as for all shares.
setup.skip_hint: The Smart Mover never touches it.
setup.help_global: Age, which time counts and how full the pool must be: the rules for every share. A share's own rule replaces the one here.
setup.help_files: What always stays where it is: lists in files (one path per line, e.g. EmbyCache's) and my own lines. A folder keeps everything below it, a pattern like *.nfo matches names, other words anywhere in the path. With Jack Emby hired, his list belongs here — otherwise I'd move his films back.
setup.help_shares: Each share can be left out, or have its own age, time and fill; its lists of what stays come on top of those for all shares. Shares with nothing to move are listed for completeness.
setup.help_save: I check every value and write smart_mover.ini anew. Not while a run of mine is going. Nothing moves until you start it, or my schedule does.
help.what_text: I run the Smart Mover: per share it looks for files older than the age you set, leaves out what is on a list, looks at how full the pool is, and hands the rest to Unraid's own move program — which decides the disk, respects the split level and skips files in use. I never copy a file myself.
help.list: Shows every share with its direction and the rules that hold for it — reads only the settings.
help.dry: Shows per share which files would move — reads the pool (and for prefer shares the array), changes nothing.
help.run: Moves for real. Only while Unraid's own mover schedule is off, never while Unraid's mover or one of Jack Emby's runs is at work. If Unraid's mover starts meanwhile, I stop before the next share.
help.rules_text: Age (in days, by ctime or mtime), the pool's fill (on ZFS the whole pool) and the lists of what stays — for all shares, or per share. Prefer shares come back to their pool with age 0 unless a share says otherwise.
help.unraid_text: Unraid's own mover takes everything a share allows. Real runs of mine only go while its schedule is ⟦Disabled⟧ — I switch it off for you if you want (exactly as its page does). ⟦Move now⟧ by hand stays possible.
help.emby_text: Jack Emby keeps what is watched next on the pool. While he is with us, his list (EmbyCache's) must be among my lists of what stays — then neither of us undoes the other's work. We never run at the same time.
help.schedule_text: Once a night is enough for most servers. A scheduled run that finds Unraid's mover at work waits up to 2 h; one refused (Unraid's schedule on) is counted, not repeated as a new line.
